# Which standard, which source, which order

<!-- generated by python/scripts/48_standards_doc.py from committed files; do not edit -->

> **Synthetic data.** Every number here comes from synthetic records, so it shows how the choices differ, not how often each is right on real patients ([how scoring works](scoring.md)).

Finding gum disease in dental records (phenotyping) means making three choices, and each one changes the answer:

1. **The definition:** what counts as gum disease, and how bad.
2. **The sources:** which parts of the record to read.
3. **The order:** which source to believe when they disagree.

## 1. The definitions

| Definition | Made for | Answers | Needs | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **2017 AAP/EFP** (Tonetti et al. 2018, [references](references.md) item 7) | Clinical care: stage, grade and extent | healthy, gingivitis, stage I–IV | a full chart: attachment loss, pocket depth, bleeding, bone loss, teeth lost to gum disease | `labels.label_chart` |
| **2012 CDC/AAP** (Eke et al., [references](references.md) item 35) | Counting it in populations (NHANES) | none, mild, moderate, severe | attachment loss and pocket depth between teeth, on different teeth; no bleeding | `sites.cdc_aap` |
| **ACES** ([action item B8](action_items.md)) | Research on chart data: the 2017 system from charts alone, with published variants for stage III vs IV | as 2017 | the chart only | `aces.py` |

### Where they disagree, on the same synthetic visits

Every one of the 2,990 synthetic visits with a gum chart, out of 3,794 in the full synthetic set, classified both ways. This is a larger set than the 223 review charts the methods are scored on, because the definitions need only the chart. 2017 AAP/EFP (rows) against 2012 CDC/AAP (columns), from `data/sites/aap_vs_cdc.csv`:

| 2017 ↓ / CDC/AAP → | none | mild | moderate | severe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Healthy | 808 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Gingivitis | 604 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| Stage I | 613 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Stage II | 469 | 106 | 7 | 0 |
| Stage III | 15 | 2 | 178 | 149 |
| Stage IV | 0 | 0 | 13 | 25 |

- **Stage I never meets CDC/AAP:** 100% of stage I visits are "none" under CDC/AAP, because it needs attachment loss of 3 mm or more on two teeth. So 2017 counts more people as having gum disease, and prevalence from the two can't be compared directly ([action item B6](action_items.md)).
- **ACES agrees with the 2017 worksheet on 2,788 of 2,990 charted visits** (`data/sites/aap_vs_aces.csv`). It moves some stage III to II, and some stage IV to III when teeth are lost but enough opposing pairs remain.

## 2. The sources

How each part of the record (gum chart, note, exam form, diagnosis codes, procedure codes, X-ray reading) is turned into a status, and what it can and can't say: [evidence_rules.md](evidence_rules.md).

## 3. The orders

When sources disagree, a rule set takes the first one, in a fixed order, that gives an answer.

| Order | Where it comes from | Believes first … last | Tested against experts? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Patel et al. 2022** | Published ([PMC9788909](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9788909); [references](references.md) item 4) | the clinician's recorded diagnosis → notes → gum chart; each only fills gaps | No: only the chart and note methods were checked, not the order |
| **The study design's** (`algorithm_design`) | This repo's own (spec 005): Patel et al. 2022 has no exam-form step ([action item A2](action_items.md)) | exam form → diagnosis codes (done, then planned) → note → gum measurements | Not yet |
| **This repo's** (`algorithm_v0`) | Its own placeholder | gum measurements → note → diagnosis codes → exam form → procedure codes; the X-ray reading can only raise the stage | Not yet |

On the 223 synthetic review charts, measurements first agrees with the answer key on 207 and exam form first on 176, scored as the leaderboard is ([results](results.md)): at five status groups, with healthy and gingivitis as one, and with a treatment plan that has no gum-disease code read as healthy or gingivitis ([presets](presets.md)). That gap flatters measurements first: the answer key was made from the measurements ([how scoring works](scoring.md)). On real records, which order is best is an open question.

## 4. Where the sources disagree

Each pair of sources, on the synthetic visits where both give a status, least agreeing first (`data/datasets/method_agreement.csv`). **Kappa:** 1 means they always agree, 0 means no better than chance. On synthetic records the generator decides how often sources disagree ([evidence_rules.md](evidence_rules.md#where-the-noise-comes-from-in-the-synthetic-data)).

## 5. Decisions still open

From [action_items.md](action_items.md), for the study lead:

- **A2:** keep the exam-form and procedure diagnosis-codes steps (Patel et al. 2022 has neither), and whether codes on planned treatment count with done treatment.
- **A3:** which order to use on real records, chosen with real reviewers, not simulated ones.
- **A5, A6:** whether procedure codes stay out, and whether the X-ray reading comes in.
- **B6, F5:** report prevalence under CDC/AAP next to 2017, so it can be compared with NHANES.
- **B8:** confirm the ACES rules against the primary paper, and choose its stage IV rule.
